qs.q: A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with neurological ataxia and ophthalmoplegia. Which water-soluble vitamin deficiency causes Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome by disrupting cellular carbohydrate oxidation?
o: Riboflavin deficiency leading to angular cheilitis
Thiamine deficiency causing Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
Niacin deficiency resulting in systemic pellagra
Cobalamin deficiency producing megaloblastic anemia
Pyridoxine deficiency causing peripheral neuropathy
qs.e: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency impairs key Krebs cycle enzymes, leading to central nervous system damage.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Nutrition and Dietetics Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs

qs.q: A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome due to a specific vitamin deficiency. Which multi-enzyme complex in energy metabolism loses crucial catalytic activity?
o: Glycogen phosphorylase catalytic dimer complex
Cytochrome c oxidase terminal pump complex
ATP synthase rotor catalytic head complex
Pyruvate dehydrogenase active enzyme complex
Citrate synthase condensation enzyme complex
qs.e: Thiamine pyrophosphate is an essential cofactor for the pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Biochemistry Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with severe Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome due to thiamine deficiency. Which key multienzyme complex is directly impaired, leading to neurological symptoms?
o: Glucose-6-phosphatase located in the hepatic endoplasmic reticulum
Glycogen phosphorylase residing within skeletal muscle fibers
ATP-citrate lyase functioning in cytosolic lipid metabolism
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I located in liver mitochondria
Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex operating in cerebral neurons
qs.e: Thiamine pyrophosphate is an essential coenzyme for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Biochemistry Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with neurological symptoms due to Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, caused by a deficiency in thiamine pyrophosphate. Which key metabolic multi-enzyme complex is directly impaired?
o: Glycogen phosphorylase complex regulating hepatic glycogenolysis breakdown rates
ATP synthase rotary complex generating cellular energy across membranes
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase initiating urea synthesis inside liver cells
Glucose 6 phosphate dehydrogenase controlling pentose phosphate pathway flux
Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex linking glycolysis pathways to citric acid cycles
qs.e: Thiamine pyrophosphate is an essential coenzyme for the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Biochemistry Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A chronic alcoholic develops Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome. This condition is primarily due to a deficiency of which vitamin?
o: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid)
qs.e: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, often seen in chronic alcoholics, is caused by thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency. The note explicitly links 'Wernicke-Korsakoff (thiamine deficiency)'.
